results.description: The non-quantized accelerated gradient method (AGM) [17] demonstrates the best performance (lower dual function value) compared to Algorithm 3.
results.evidence:
Two Gaussian run output files found:
1. results/formal/gaussian_er_constant/metrics.json (10-node Erdos-Renyi, 5000 iterations): AGM final_dual_value = -0.6957470758833869, PPS (Algorithm 3) final_dual_value = -0.6848345504907407. AGM is lower (better).
2. results/formal/gaussian_topology_m30/metrics.json (30-node topology, 5000 iterations): AGM final_dual_value = -0.30955818870831997, PPS (Algorithm 3) final_dual_value = -0.18998126448324573. AGM is lower (better).
In both Gaussian experiments, AGM achieves a lower dual function value than Algorithm 3 (PPS), confirming the required order AGM > Algorithm 3 under lower_is_better.
results.note: The Algorithm 3 method is labeled 'PPS' in the output files. Both available Gaussian datasets confirm the ranking. The claim holds in all observed Gaussian run outputs.

results.description: The non-quantized accelerated gradient method (AGM) [17] demonstrates the best performance (lower consensus gap) compared to Algorithm 3.
results.evidence: No output file named "exp1_gaussian_wb" was found. The two available Gaussian run outputs are results/formal/gaussian_er_constant/metrics.json and results/formal/gaussian_topology_m30/metrics.json. Both compare AGM vs. PPS (which maps to Algorithm 3) on Gaussian data. In gaussian_er_constant: AGM final_consensus_gap=0.000420, PPS=0.0500. In gaussian_topology_m30: AGM final_consensus_gap=0.00136, PPS=0.0486. In both cases AGM < PPS (lower_is_better), confirming AGM is strictly better (lower consensus gap) than Algorithm 3 (PPS), satisfying the required order AGM > Algorithm 3.
results.note: The experiment_id "exp1_gaussian_wb" does not exist as a named output; the verdict is based on the two available Gaussian outputs. "PPS" in the outputs is identified as Algorithm 3 from the CLAIMS.json description ("decentralized accelerated primal-dual PPS" vs "dense non-quantized AGM baseline"). Confidence is medium because of the experiment-ID mismatch.

results.description: Algorithm 3 with M_t = 1 and r_t = 10 converges to the barycenter with significantly less communication overhead than AGM.
results.evidence: No run output with experiment_id "exp1_gaussian_wb" or with the specific hyperparameters M_t=1, r_t=10 was found anywhere in the repository. The available Gaussian run outputs are: (1) results/formal/gaussian_er_constant/metrics.json — config has quantization_samples=10 and gamma=0.1, method labeled "PPS", PPS=13,316,423 bits vs AGM=1,292,800,000 bits; (2) results/formal/gaussian_topology_m30/metrics.json — config has quantization_samples=10 and gamma=0.1, method labeled "PPS", PPS=5,792,644 bits vs AGM=562,368,000 bits. Neither experiment matches the required M_t=1, r_t=10 configuration. No other result files, logs, CSV, or JSON mentioning exp1_gaussian_wb, M_t=1, or r_t=10 were found. CLAIM_RESULTS.json does not reference this experiment either.
results.note: The available runs do show the quantized algorithm (PPS) using ~97x fewer communication bits than AGM on Gaussian datasets, but those are different hyperparameter settings (M_t=10 samples, gamma=0.1) and different experiment IDs from the one specified in the rubric (exp1_gaussian_wb with M_t=1, r_t=10). The ranking claim may well be directionally correct, but the specific experiment's run outputs are absent.

results.description: Algorithm 3 with M_t = 1 and r_t = 10 can rapidly converge to the Gaussian Wasserstein barycenter.
results.evidence: Two Gaussian Wasserstein barycenter experiments were found: results/formal/gaussian_er_constant/metrics.json and results/formal/gaussian_topology_m30/metrics.json. Both use PPS (Algorithm 3) with quantization_samples=10 (r_t=10). In gaussian_er_constant (10 nodes, 5000 iterations): PPS final_consensus_gap=0.0500 (starting from 1.14 at iter=1, still 0.096 at iter=1250/5000), vs AGM final=0.00042 — PPS is ~120× worse and still slowly decreasing at run end. In gaussian_topology_m30 (30 nodes, 1500 iterations): PPS final_consensus_gap=0.0486 vs AGM=0.00136 (~35× worse). The CLAIM_RESULTS.json explicitly notes the wasserstein-barycenter-application claim is "partially_reproduced" with observation that "PPS reduces disagreement but remains noisier than dense AGM at the recorded horizons." The run outputs do not support "rapid convergence" — PPS shows slow, noisy convergence still far from the barycenter at all recorded horizons. Additionally, the config files do not explicitly show M_t=1 as a parameter.
results.note: The configs show quantization_samples=10 (plausibly r_t=10) but no explicit M_t=1 setting. The convergence shown in outputs is qualitatively the opposite of rapid — the PPS consensus gap decreases very slowly and remains orders of magnitude above AGM throughout all runs.

results.description: Algorithm 3 with constant batch size r_t and M_t ≪ n achieves similar visual quality of the approximate barycentre to AGM on the MNIST experiment.
results.evidence: results/formal/mnist_digit2_100x100/metrics.json and resolved_config.json confirm: constant batch_size r_t=20, quantization_samples M_t=10, image support n=10,000 (100×100), so M_t/n=0.001≪1. PPS final dual value=0.8892644896 vs AGM final dual=0.8883248821 (relative gap 0.106%). Pixel-level comparison of barycenter.npz arrays (40 nodes × 10,000 pixels): mean absolute normalized pixel diff=4.52e-5, max=3.11e-4 — essentially identical visual outputs. run.log confirms these outputs were produced by the experiment. PPS used only ~4.6M bits vs AGM's ~22B bits while yielding the same approximate barycenter image.
results.note: The 'similar visual quality' claim is supported both by the near-identical dual objective values (0.106% relative gap) and by the very small pixel-level differences in the stored barycenter arrays. The figure_convergence.png is also present but not directly inspected (numerical data is sufficient).
